hero.headline: Apple redesigns Siri to reduce unnecessary responses
hero.body:
Apple unveiled a fundamentally rebuilt version of Siri at its Worldwide Developers Conference, marking a major shift in how the voice assistant operates. The new system, powered by Google's Gemini AI model through a billion-dollar partnership, integrates with Apple Intelligence and will roll out to consumers in the fall.

Mike Rockwell, Apple's vice-president of Siri engineering, demonstrated how the redesigned assistant has become more conversational and capable of handling complex tasks across Apple's native app ecosystem. In one demonstration, Rockwell showed Siri identifying a beach location from a photo, retrieving a friend's address, and providing directions with a planned stop, all within a single interface rather than jumping between multiple apps.

A key improvement in the new Siri is its ability to determine when responses are necessary. Rather than providing verbose answers to every query, the assistant delivers more concise replies, avoiding unnecessary chatter that plagued earlier versions. This represents a departure from many AI chatbots that tend toward wordiness and excessive politeness.

The expanded capabilities will eventually include proofreading, shopping assistance, calendar management, and image analysis for tasks like retrieving nutritional information from photos of food. Initially, the tool will only support English. A dedicated Siri app will house these features alongside integration into Safari, text messaging, and the Home app.

Craig Federighi, Apple's senior vice-president of software engineering, acknowledged the company's earlier lag in the AI race, noting that some competitors appear to be "pursuing AI for the sake of AI, without clear regard for the people that it's ultimately meant to serve." Apple has repeatedly delayed Siri updates since first announcing improvements in 2024, and the company faced legal consequences when it agreed to pay 250 million dollars in May to settle a class-action lawsuit alleging false advertising of Siri's capabilities.

Alongside the Siri overhaul, Apple announced enhanced child safety features. The company introduced new tools allowing parents to restrict content, control who children communicate with, and limit app access. An updated setup assistant helps parents gradually expand permissions as children age. New monitoring capabilities can blur violent or explicit messages, and parents can set daily time allowances for specific apps using their own preferences or recommendations from the American Academy of Pediatrics.

These safety features arrived amid increased scrutiny over image manipulation apps and government pressure to protect minors online. UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer urged Apple and Google to activate built-in features preventing children from accessing sexually explicit content.

The changes reflect Apple's strategy of positioning privacy and thoughtful AI integration as differentiators against competitors who rely more heavily on cloud-based processing. The new Siri will reach developers through beta versions and consumers later this year.

cards.headline: US and Iran Exchange Strikes Across Middle East for Second Consecutive Day
cards.body:
The United States and Iran engaged in direct military exchanges for a second day, with the conflict expanding to involve Israel and raising serious concerns about broader regional warfare in the Middle East.

Israel launched airstrikes on Iran following Iranian missile attacks on northern Israel, marking the first direct exchange between the two countries since a ceasefire agreement on April 8. The Israeli military struck Iranian military installations, including a petrochemical complex, and said it dismantled Iranian defense systems across multiple locations. Iranian state television reported explosions in Isfahan, Karaj, Tabriz, and Tehran. The Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps responded by targeting two military bases in Israel as part of Operation Victory, or "Nasr."

The strikes intensified an already volatile situation. Yemen's Houthi rebels, aligned with Iran, fired missiles at Israel and announced a complete ban on Israeli shipping in the Red Sea, threatening to disrupt a crucial global trade route. Missile fragments from Iranian attacks caused damage to homes in a West Bank settlement, though no injuries were reported.

The conflict has created significant diplomatic complications. According to a senior US official, President Trump called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu before the Iranian attack to urge restraint and delay any retaliation. However, Israel proceeded with strikes anyway. Trump publicly called for both countries to stop their attacks, writing on his Truth Social platform: "Israel and Iran must immediately stop 'shooting'."

Iranian officials rejected suggestions that Netanyahu acted independently from the United States. A foreign ministry spokesperson stated that "no one believes that the Zionist regime would carry out any action without prior coordination and cooperation with the United States." Some Iranian analysts pointed to what they described as video evidence of American involvement, noting that Israel lacks certain long-range cruise missile capabilities attributed to US naval assets in the eastern Mediterranean.

The White House did not respond to inquiries about whether it coordinated with Israel or approved the strikes. This ambiguity has complicated ongoing peace negotiations between the US and Iran, which had been stalled. Iranian hardliners in parliament had already pressured negotiators to abandon talks, and suspicions about American involvement could further derail diplomatic efforts.

The escalating military exchanges rattled global markets. Brent crude oil jumped 3.50 dollars to 96.59 dollars per barrel, while Asian stock markets fell sharply in early trading as investors reacted to potential disruptions in Middle Eastern oil supplies and regional stability.

The geographic spread of the military strikes, spanning from Iran to Israel to the Persian Gulf, underscores how quickly the conflict has expanded beyond bilateral tensions. Military observers warned that the situation bears similarities to previous periods of acute US-Iran hostility, though the current direct military exchanges between multiple nations represent a potentially more dangerous phase with significant consequences for regional stability.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Jump After U.S. Launches Second Day of Strikes on Iran
cards.body:
Oil prices surged following a second consecutive day of military strikes between the United States and Iran, intensifying concerns about a potential escalation in the Middle East. The renewed conflict has rattled global energy markets already dealing with multiple sources of uncertainty.

The escalation began after a U.S. Army Apache helicopter went down near the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday morning. President Trump stated that Iran was responsible for downing the aircraft, though U.S. officials told Reuters the helicopter collided with an Iranian drone and the circumstances remain under investigation. Trump directed the military to launch strikes beginning at 10pm UK time on Tuesday in response to the incident. U.S. Central Command said the strikes targeted radar and air defense facilities along the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran responded with its own barrage of attacks on Wednesday morning. The country's Revolutionary Guards struck the U.S. al-Azraq base in Jordan with long-range missiles, according to Iranian media reports. Iran also said it had launched drone attacks at bases in Kuwait and Bahrain, targeting F-35 fighter jet hangars and command-and-control centers. U.S. officials stated that nearly all missiles and drones launched by Iran were intercepted. Jordan's armed forces said they shot down five missiles before impact.

Despite the military exchanges, U.S. officials signaled they were not seeking full-scale war with Iran. Centcom called the operation "a proportional response to unjustified Iranian aggression." Trump himself downplayed the helicopter incident in a Wall Street Journal interview, saying it "wasn't a big deal" and that the pilot was fine. The helicopter's two crew members were rescued in an unprecedented operation using an unmanned drone boat.

The Strait of Hormuz remains critical to global energy supplies, with roughly one-fifth of the world's petroleum passing through the waterway. Any sustained military engagement threatens shipping routes and could constrain global supply, directly pushing prices higher.

The conflict erupts as diplomatic negotiations appear stalled. Trump had earlier expressed optimism about reaching a deal with Iran within days, but those hopes dimmed after the helicopter incident. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned on social media that Iran "will leave no attack or threat unanswered" and told the U.S. to "leave our region if you want to be safe."

This latest exchange follows months of tension since the U.S. and Iran agreed to an initial ceasefire in April. The broader U.S.-Israel campaign against Iran since late February has already shaken global markets and pushed up energy prices and food costs worldwide.

Markets will likely focus on whether military exchanges continue, whether diplomatic channels reopen, and whether other nations become involved in the escalating conflict.

cards.headline: Consumer Prices Rose 4.2% in May, Highest in Three Years
cards.teaser: Inflation reached its highest annual rate in three years, with consumer prices climbing 4.2% in May.
cards.body:
Consumer prices increased 4.2% on an annual basis in May, marking the highest inflation rate the United States has seen in three years. The acceleration in price growth comes as the country faces economic pressures from the ongoing U.S.-Israel military operations in Iran, which have contributed to rising costs across multiple sectors.

President Trump responded to questions about the inflation figures by stating he loves the inflation, a departure from typical political responses to rising prices. Consumers are increasingly feeling the financial strain as the cost of living climbs, with the conflict in Iran adding to economic uncertainty and upward pressure on prices for goods and services.

cards.headline: Trump pushes for $350 billion Pentagon spending increase in new bill
cards.teaser: The president called on Republicans to pass a third reconciliation bill that would include a major defense budget infusion and election law changes.
cards.body:
President Trump demanded that Republicans pass a third reconciliation bill including a $350 billion increase in Pentagon spending and an overhaul of election procedures. The president referred to the legislation as the Save America Act.

Top Republican appropriators in the Senate pushed back on the proposal, saying a third reconciliation bill is not an option. The resistance from senior members of his own party suggests the legislation faces significant hurdles. Reconciliation bills allow the Senate to pass measures with a simple majority, bypassing the usual 60-vote threshold.

cards.headline: Trump casts doubt on renewing U.S.-Mexico-Canada trade agreement
cards.teaser: The president said he may not renew the USMCA, the trade deal he negotiated during his first term to replace NAFTA.
cards.body:
President Trump said Wednesday he may not renew the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement, the free trade deal he created during his first term as a replacement for NAFTA. Trump told reporters he was not looking to extend the pact.

The USMCA sets the terms of trade between the three North American countries and was a major accomplishment of Trump's initial presidency. The agreement includes a review process that permits the countries to renegotiate or exit the deal.

cards.headline: Ukrainian Strikes Target Russian Military Facilities Deep Inside Russia
cards.teaser: Ukraine launched missile and drone attacks on Russian military installations, including facilities in St. Petersburg.
cards.body:
Ukraine's military struck a Russian military plant located deep within Russian territory, extending its reach far beyond border regions. The country also targeted a Russian oil refinery and attacked a "shadow fleet" oil tanker in the Black Sea.

These strikes are part of Ukraine's broader campaign to disrupt Russian supply lines and military capabilities. By hitting oil facilities and infrastructure used to support Russian operations, Kyiv has made it increasingly difficult for Moscow to provision both its military forces and the territories it occupies.

cards.headline: Anti-Immigrant Riots Erupt in Belfast Following Stabbing Attack
cards.teaser: Police deployed water cannons against rioters in Northern Ireland as violence spread through Belfast neighborhoods.
cards.body:
A stabbing incident in Belfast triggered two nights of violent disorder across Northern Ireland. Rioters set fires, including vehicles and a bus, and threw bricks and bottles at police. Law enforcement responded with water cannons to disperse crowds as violence spread through multiple neighborhoods.

The unrest forced families to evacuate their homes. The disturbances represent part of a broader wave of anti-immigrant violence affecting the United Kingdom, with authorities working to restore order in affected areas.

cards.headline: Senior Russian Military Official Killed in Car Bombing Near Moscow
cards.teaser: A car bomb killed a high-ranking Russian military official in an explosion near the Russian capital.
cards.body:
A senior Russian military official died in a car bombing near Moscow. The explosion killed an ammunition chief for the Russian military, according to reports describing the official as a missile chief who died in a fiery blast.

Russian authorities are investigating two car bombs in Moscow. The attack represents the latest in a series of targeted strikes against Russian military personnel, with the explosion occurring in the vicinity of the capital rather than in conflict zones where Russian forces are actively engaged.

cards.headline: Ukraine War Surpasses Length of World War I
cards.teaser: The conflict in Ukraine has now lasted longer than World War I, with parallels in the grinding nature of combat.
cards.body:
The conflict in Ukraine has now lasted longer than World War I, which spanned from 1914 to 1918. Like the earlier war, the current conflict has been characterized by grinding, attritional combat that has reshaped how warfare is conducted.

Modern technology plays a central role in the Ukraine war, with ground-based drones becoming key to battlefield operations. Ukraine has increasingly relied on robotic warfare to enhance its military capabilities, shifting frontline duties from soldiers to unmanned systems that allow the country to punch above its weight against a larger adversary.

cards.headline: Indonesian Military Court Sentences Four Over Acid Attack on Rights Advocate
cards.teaser: Four people received sentences for an acid attack on an outspoken critic of Indonesia's military.
cards.body:
An Indonesian military court sentenced four individuals in connection with an acid attack on a human rights advocate. The victim is an outspoken critic of Indonesia's powerful military, and military prosecutors took over the case despite objections from the victim.

The case has drawn attention to the role of military courts in Indonesia and the treatment of critics of the armed forces. The victim had opposed the military's handling of the prosecution, raising questions about the appropriate jurisdiction for cases involving attacks on civilian critics of military institutions.

cards.headline: Dispute Emerges Over Cause of Air India Flight 171 Crash
cards.teaser: A contentious disagreement has developed over what led to the crash of an Air India flight.
cards.body:
Investigators are engaged in a furious dispute over what caused Air India Flight 171 to crash. The disagreement centers on determining the factors that led to the aircraft going down.

The investigation's final conclusions have not yet been published, though additional details may emerge in the coming days.

hero.headline: Teachers across U.S. take second jobs as economic pressures mount
hero.body:
Teachers across the United States are increasingly working second jobs to make ends meet as economic pressures intensify. The trend reflects broader financial strain on educators whose salaries have struggled to keep pace with rising living costs.

The development comes amid what has been characterized as a tough economy for American workers. Teachers, whose base salaries vary widely by state and district, have long faced compensation challenges relative to other professions requiring similar education levels. The current economic climate has made these disparities more acute.

Many educators are supplementing their teaching income with evening and weekend work. The second jobs range from retail positions to tutoring to gig economy work. The additional employment places extra demands on teachers who already face significant workloads from classroom instruction, lesson planning, and grading.

The issue affects teachers at all grade levels and in various regions of the country. School districts nationwide have reported difficulties recruiting and retaining teachers, with compensation cited as a major factor. Some states have moved to increase teacher pay in recent years, but implementation has been uneven.

The broader economic context includes rising costs for housing, healthcare, and other essentials that have outpaced wage growth in many sectors. For teachers, whose salaries are often set by multi-year contracts and public budgets, adjusting to rapid economic changes can be particularly difficult.

The staffing challenges are evident in recruitment trends. The number of newly qualified teachers entering the profession has reached historic lows. The shortage is particularly acute in specialized subjects, where non-specialist teachers are filling gaps in classrooms.

Workplace departures have also contributed to staffing pressures. While some progress has been made in retaining educators, the overall teaching workforce continues to face strain. Schools serving disadvantaged communities have been especially affected by teacher shortages.

Government efforts to address the crisis have had mixed results. Some initiatives have aimed to recruit additional teachers in key subject areas, though the pace of hiring has not consistently matched stated goals. Policymakers have pointed to funding constraints and budget limitations as obstacles to rapid expansion of the teaching workforce.

Education experts have emphasized the urgency of sustained action to reverse the effects of teacher shortages. The quality of instruction, particularly in mathematics and other critical subjects, depends on having adequate numbers of qualified educators. Without significant improvement in working conditions and compensation, the profession risks continued attrition.

The situation raises questions about the sustainability of the teaching profession and whether schools can maintain adequate staffing levels if financial pressures continue to drive educators toward other careers or force them to work multiple jobs to remain in the field. Addressing these challenges will likely require coordinated efforts involving increased funding, competitive salaries, and improved workplace conditions.

cards.headline: Knicks overcome 29-point deficit to take 3-1 NBA Finals lead
cards.teaser: New York rallied from a record deficit to beat San Antonio 107-106 and move within one win of their first championship since 1973.
cards.body:
The New York Knicks completed the largest comeback in NBA Finals history, erasing a 29-point deficit to beat the San Antonio Spurs 107-106 on Wednesday night. OG Anunoby hit the game-winning tip-in with 1.2 seconds remaining off a Jalen Brunson missed three-pointer.

The victory gives New York a commanding 3-1 series lead and puts them one win away from their first championship since 1973. The Knicks will have a chance to clinch the title in the next game.

cards.headline: ActBlue CEO invokes Fifth Amendment repeatedly in House testimony
cards.teaser: The chief executive of the Democratic fundraising platform refused to answer questions during a congressional hearing.
cards.body:
The chief executive of ActBlue, a Democratic fundraising platform, repeatedly invoked Fifth Amendment protections against self-incrimination while testifying before a House panel investigating the organization's practices.

The CEO published an opinion piece explaining the decision to invoke Fifth Amendment rights during the congressional hearing. House Democrats responded to the Republican-led investigation by threatening to scrutinize WinRed, the Republican equivalent fundraising platform.

cards.headline: Democrats weigh support for GOP Senate candidate Platner
cards.teaser: Republicans are using the progressive candidate's nomination against Democrats as he prepares to face Senator Susan Collins in Maine.
cards.body:
Democrats are reluctantly accepting Graham Platner as the Republican nominee for Senate in Maine, where he will face incumbent Senator Susan Collins. Republicans are wielding Platner's candidacy as a political weapon against Democrats, highlighting his progressive positions.

Platner clinched the Republican nomination and immediately attacked his own party in remarks following the primary. His candidacy has drawn comparisons to both Bernie Sanders and Donald Trump, with some characterizing him as a protest vote. Some opinion writers have argued that Maine Democrats should back Collins, the Republican incumbent, over the GOP challenger.

cards.headline: Trump says he 'loves the inflation' as prices rise at fastest rate in three years
cards.teaser: The president made the comment as consumers face increased strain from rising prices linked to conflict in the Middle East.
cards.body:
President Trump expressed support for rising inflation, saying "I love the inflation" after new data showed prices jumped to 4.2% annually in May—the highest rate in three years. The increase marks the third consecutive monthly rise since the U.S. and Israel launched military operations against Iran.

Speaking from the White House on Wednesday, Trump indicated he was unconcerned about inflation due to recent developments in the conflict. Inflation had stood at 2.4% before the war began, but the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has driven up energy prices significantly.

cards.headline: U.S. and Iran exchange strikes for second consecutive day
cards.teaser: American forces targeted military sites in southern Iran, while Tehran responded by striking U.S. assets in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan.
cards.body:
The United States launched strikes against military targets across multiple Iranian cities on the second consecutive day of escalating conflict. Iran responded by attacking American military assets in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan. Kuwait subsequently closed its airspace following the strikes.

Defense Secretary Hegseth stated the U.S. would "negotiate with bombs" if necessary. Negotiations to end the broader regional conflict have stalled, with Iran maintaining control over the Strait of Hormuz. Israel has warned of potential missile launches from Lebanon as tensions continue to intensify across the Middle East.

cards.headline: Medicare Advantage Plans Frequently Deny Seniors Access to Nursing Home and Rehab Care
cards.teaser: Federal investigators found Medicare Advantage plans routinely reject requests for short-term nursing home and inpatient rehabilitation services.
cards.body:
Two U.S. government reports document that Medicare Advantage plans frequently reject requests for short-term nursing home care and inpatient rehabilitation services. These denials affect seniors seeking specialized care after hospitalizations or medical events that require intensive recovery.

Medicare Advantage, the private insurance alternative to traditional Medicare, serves millions of seniors nationwide. The reports suggest that cost containment practices by private insurers may be restricting access to medically necessary care that traditional Medicare would typically cover.

cards.headline: Frasers Group Offers $1.73 Billion to Acquire Full Ownership of Hugo Boss
cards.teaser: Mike Ashley's retail group has made a bid to buy the remaining shares of German fashion brand Hugo Boss.
cards.body:
Frasers Group, controlled by Mike Ashley, has made a £1.73 billion offer to acquire full ownership of Hugo Boss. The British retail company currently owns just over a quarter of the German fashion brand and is seeking to purchase the remaining shares.

The bid would give Frasers complete control of Hugo Boss, the established luxury menswear and fashion brand with global reach.

cards.headline: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei Operates With Single Direct Report
cards.teaser: The head of AI company Anthropic has structured his leadership with just one direct report, an unusual approach compared to other tech executives.
cards.body:
Dario Amodei, chief executive of artificial intelligence company Anthropic, has organized his management structure with only one direct report. This stands in sharp contrast to other technology executives, such as Nvidia's Jensen Huang, who manages 60 direct reports. Amodei reportedly spends roughly 40% of his time on company culture rather than product development.

The CEO has delegated operational responsibilities to his sister while focusing primarily on AI strategy and organizational culture. Amodei has stated that culture, rather than products alone, will determine which company wins in the competitive artificial intelligence sector. The streamlined reporting structure reflects a deliberate management philosophy at Anthropic as it competes with other major AI firms.

cards.headline: Anthropic Reverses Policy After Backlash From AI Researchers Using Claude
cards.teaser: The AI company walked back a policy change that drew criticism from researchers working with its Claude language model.
cards.body:
Anthropic reversed a policy that could have disrupted work by AI researchers using its Claude language model. The company had introduced restrictions with its new Fable 5 model that prompted immediate backlash from users and researchers who rely on the technology for their work.

Microsoft subsequently limited employee use of Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 over data retention concerns, according to reports. The policy reversal came shortly after the company announced that Claude Fable 5 would be available through Microsoft Foundry, positioning the model as a tool for powering autonomous agents. The swift change suggests Anthropic is balancing security and usage restrictions with the need to maintain its user base.

cards.headline: Asian Stock Markets Decline Following Wall Street Tech Sell-Off
cards.teaser: Asian shares fell after technology stocks extended losses on Wall Street, while oil prices rose amid U.S. strikes on Iran.
cards.body:
Stock markets across Asia retreated following another day of losses for technology stocks on Wall Street. The decline in chip-related and AI stocks in the United States carried over into Asian trading sessions, weighing on investor sentiment in the region. Oil prices moved higher during Asian trading hours as markets responded to U.S. military strikes against Iran.

The combination of technology sector weakness and geopolitical tensions contributed to a risk-off mood among investors. Asian chip-linked shares showed some recovery after their U.S. counterparts bounced back from earlier lows, though overall market confidence remained subdued. The mixed signals reflect ongoing uncertainty about both the technology sector's near-term prospects and the trajectory of the U.S.-Iran conflict.

cards.headline: Former xAI engineer sues over alleged firing for safety concerns
cards.teaser: A lawsuit claims the AI company terminated an engineer who raised alarms about its Grok chatbot just before SpaceX's initial public offering.
cards.body:
A former xAI engineer has sued the company and SpaceX, claiming he was terminated for raising safety concerns about the Grok artificial intelligence system. According to the lawsuit, the firing occurred days before SpaceX's initial public offering.

The legal action alleges wrongful termination related to the engineer's warnings about potential risks associated with the Grok chatbot.

cards.headline: Cold water anomaly in Atlantic may signal ocean current weakening
cards.teaser: Scientists say an unusual cold region in the Atlantic Ocean could indicate the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation is approaching a critical threshold.
cards.body:
Researchers have identified a persistent cold area in the Atlantic Ocean that suggests the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation may be weakening. The phenomenon, referred to as a cold blob, stands in contrast to warming trends observed across most ocean regions. Scientists view the anomaly as a potential indicator that the AMOC is nearing a tipping point.

The AMOC is a system of ocean currents that transports warm water northward and cold water southward, playing a major role in regulating climate patterns. A weakening of this circulation could alter weather patterns across North America and Europe. The cold blob's presence has prompted increased monitoring and research into the stability of Atlantic ocean currents.

cards.headline: Ubisoft closes studios in San Francisco and Winnipeg
cards.teaser: The video game publisher is shutting down multiple locations as part of an organizational restructuring, affecting up to 380 employees.
cards.body:
Ubisoft announced the closure of studios in San Francisco and Winnipeg as part of a larger restructuring effort. The Winnipeg location employed approximately 65 people. Across multiple closures, the company will eliminate up to 380 positions.

The closures represent the latest round of layoffs at the video game publisher, which has been reorganizing its operations. Reports indicate Ubisoft placed embargoes on some journalists covering the layoffs. The company has not provided a detailed timeline for the studio closures or outlined specific reasons for selecting these locations.

cards.headline: Framework postpones Laptop 13 Pro shipments to July
cards.teaser: The modular computer maker delayed its first Laptop 13 Pro deliveries by a month to address software issues discovered during final testing.
cards.body:
Framework has delayed the Laptop 13 Pro launch, pushing first batch shipments from June to July. Some orders may slip into early August depending on demand and production.

The 13-inch Laptop 13 Pro is Framework's flagship model, marking its expansion into the professional laptop segment. The company's modular design allows users to replace and upgrade individual components.

cards.headline: Study finds humans prefer walking counterclockwise in crowds
cards.teaser: Researchers documented a consistent leftward bias in pedestrian movement patterns, though the underlying cause remains unexplained.
cards.body:
A study published in Nature found that people exhibit a preference for counterclockwise motion when walking in crowds. The research identified what scientists describe as an individual locomotor bias that influences how pedestrians navigate shared spaces. The pattern held across different locations and contexts.

Researchers observed the leftward veering tendency but have not determined why this preference exists. The findings suggest an inherent aspect of human movement behavior that manifests at both individual and collective levels. The discovery could have applications in crowd management and urban design, though scientists say more research is needed to understand the mechanism driving the bias.

cards.headline: Extreme rainfall killed 7% of Tapanuli orangutan population
cards.teaser: Four days of intense rain contributed to deaths among the world's rarest orangutan species, which scientists link to climate change.
cards.body:
More than 1,000mm of rain fell over four days in North Sumatra, Indonesia in November 2025, triggering landslides that killed approximately 58 Tapanuli orangutans. This represents 7% of the entire species, which numbers around 800 individuals, and 11% of the local population.

The Tapanuli orangutan is the world's rarest great ape species and critically endangered. Researchers linked the extreme rainfall to the climate crisis, raising concerns about the species' survival as weather events become increasingly severe and frequent.

hero.headline: Knicks complete largest comeback in NBA Finals history, one win from title
hero.body:
The New York Knicks erased a 29-point deficit to defeat the San Antonio Spurs 107-106 in Game 4 of the NBA Finals, achieving the largest comeback in championship series history. The victory gives New York a commanding 3-1 series lead and puts them one win away from their first NBA title since 1973.

The Spurs controlled much of the game, with Victor Wembanyama leading San Antonio to an early double-digit advantage that ballooned to 29 points in the second quarter. The Spurs' hot three-point shooting and Wembanyama's dominant two-way play had the Madison Square Garden crowd subdued as the Knicks appeared headed toward defeat.

The momentum shifted dramatically in the fourth quarter when the Knicks unleashed a devastating 28-9 run over just more than seven minutes. New York converted defensive stops into fast-break opportunities, systematically chipping away at the deficit. Jalen Brunson drove through traffic for a layup with 1:22 remaining to give the Knicks their first lead of the game at 105-104.

The Spurs reclaimed the lead on a pair of Stephon Castle free throws, setting up the final sequence. With 1.2 seconds left, Brunson's missed three-pointer was tipped in by OG Anunoby for the game-winning basket. "Right hand from God," Knicks center Karl-Anthony Towns said of the decisive play.

The comeback electrified New York City, with thousands of fans pouring into Manhattan streets to celebrate after the final buzzer. The Knicks can clinch their first championship of the 21st century when the series returns to San Antonio for Game 5 on Saturday night.

Brunson finished with 36 points while Anunoby added 33 for New York. Wembanyama contributed 24 points, 13 rebounds, and three blocks for San Antonio in a losing effort.

The game was physical throughout, with multiple confrontations between players. Wembanyama drew a flagrant foul early in the contest and was later called for a flagrant after hitting Towns. Mitchell Robinson also had exchanges with Wembanyama during the game.

The Spurs had appeared positioned to seize control of the series after winning Game 3 and building their commanding lead early in Game 4. Instead, San Antonio faces elimination and would need to become only the second team in NBA history to overcome a 3-1 Finals deficit to avoid defeat.

The remarkable turnaround showcased the Knicks' resilience and composure under pressure on basketball's biggest stage. New York's ability to maintain belief while facing such a significant deficit proved to be the difference in one of the most memorable playoff performances in NBA history.

cards.headline: 17-year-old Cooper Lutkenhaus defeats Olympic 800m champion in Diamond League meet
cards.teaser: American runner Cooper Lutkenhaus upset Olympic gold medalist Emmanuel Wanyonyi in the men's 800 meters at the Diamond League meeting in Oslo.
cards.body:
American teenager Cooper Lutkenhaus delivered a stunning upset at the Diamond League meet in Oslo, winning the men's 800 meters by 0.01 seconds against Olympic champion Emmanuel Wanyonyi. The 17-year-old's victory represents a breakthrough performance on the international stage at the historic Bislett Stadion, a venue that has hosted 70 world records.

Fellow Australian teenager Gout Gout had a contrasting result, finishing sixth in the 200 meters. The performances highlighted the stark differences in readiness between the young athletes competing at the Diamond League level.

cards.headline: NCAA outdoor track and field championships underway
cards.teaser: The 2026 Division I outdoor track and field championships are taking place with Day 1 results determining which athletes advance to finals.
cards.body:
The NCAA Division I outdoor track and field championships are in progress, with athletes competing for national titles and All-American honors. Four Michigan Wolverines advanced to finals events after Day 1 competition, while one Wolverine earned Second Team All-American recognition. The Florida Gators are also competing for team trophies at the championships.

The multi-day event features preliminary rounds and finals across distance, sprint, field, and relay events. Athletes who place in the top eight of their events earn All-American status, while team points are tallied to determine the men's and women's national champions.

cards.headline: Knicks owner and Mayor Mamdani clash over canceled watch party outside Madison Square Garden
cards.teaser: Security concerns led to the cancellation of a planned outdoor watch party for NBA Finals Game 4, sparking a public dispute between team ownership and city officials.
cards.body:
The New York Knicks organization and Mayor Mamdani engaged in a public disagreement over security measures and the cancellation of a planned watch party outside Madison Square Garden ahead of Game 4 of the NBA Finals. The NYPD banned spontaneous gatherings outside the arena, and a previously planned watch party for fans was called off, leading to criticism from both sides.

Knicks fans still gathered outside MSG to celebrate the team's Game 4 victory despite the restrictions. Street closures were implemented around Madison Square Garden, and heightened security measures were put in place. The dispute centered on crowd control concerns and differing views about allowing public celebrations during the Finals.

cards.headline: Victor Wembanyama avoids flagrant foul for contact with Jalen Brunson in Game 4
cards.teaser: The Spurs center was assessed penalties during the Finals loss but avoided a flagrant designation for one incident involving the Knicks guard.
cards.body:
San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama avoided a flagrant foul call for contact with Knicks guard Jalen Brunson during Game 4 of the NBA Finals. Wembanyama did draw a flagrant foul early in the game and was later called for one himself after hitting Karl-Anthony Towns. The physical play characterized the Finals matchup between the teams.

Wembanyama was also seen engaging with Knicks center Mitchell Robinson during the game, reportedly telling Robinson that he was in his head. Despite the physical exchanges and Wembanyama's individual efforts, the Spurs fell in Game 4 and now face elimination in the series.

cards.headline: Colleges and athletic directors react to Texas Tech quarterback eligibility ruling
cards.teaser: A legal decision regarding quarterback Brendan Sorsby has prompted responses from coaches, athletic directors, and conference officials across college sports.
cards.body:
Coaches and athletic directors have expressed strong reactions to a ruling involving Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby's eligibility. Texas Tech booster Cody Campbell defended the program against criticism, suggesting that opponents are reluctant to face the Red Raiders because of competitive concerns.

The eligibility dispute has sparked debate across college sports conferences about how rules are applied. The situation has drawn reactions from multiple programs and conferences, highlighting broader questions about the consistency of eligibility decisions in college athletics.

cards.headline: FIFA president Infantino addresses World Cup organization for first time in three years
cards.teaser: Gianni Infantino held his first media session since 2023 but offered little reassurance about FIFA's handling of the 2026 tournament.
cards.body:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino addressed media for the first time in three years on Wednesday at Estadio Ciudad de México ahead of the 2026 World Cup. When pressed about tournament preparation concerns, he told questioners to "chill and relax" — a response that failed to address doubts about FIFA's control over World Cup logistics.

The 2026 tournament will be jointly hosted by the United States, Canada, and Mexico, with the opening match scheduled between Mexico and South Africa on Thursday. Infantino's limited media engagement in recent years has drawn criticism for a lack of transparency regarding World Cup planning and execution.

hero.headline: 24 Jump Street in Development With Original Stars in Talks to Return
hero.body:
Sony Pictures is developing 24 Jump Street, with original stars Jonah Hill, Channing Tatum, and Ice Cube in talks to return for the third installment of the action comedy franchise. The project marks a revival of the series after more than a decade since 22 Jump Street released in 2014.

The Jump Street films originated as a modern reboot of the 1980s television series of the same name. The first film, 21 Jump Street, released in 2012 and became a surprise hit, earning over $200 million worldwide. Its sequel, 22 Jump Street, surpassed that success in 2014, earning more than $330 million globally. Both films followed undercover police officers played by Hill and Tatum as they infiltrated educational institutions to solve crimes, with Ice Cube playing their commanding officer.

Plans for a third film have circulated for years, with various approaches discussed including a crossover with the Men in Black franchise. That project, which would have been titled MIB 23, was discussed publicly but never moved forward. The current development represents a return to the core Jump Street concept without the crossover element.

The original films were directed by Phil Lord and Christopher Miller, who went on to direct The Lego Movie and produce the Spider-Verse animated films. Their involvement in the new project has not been announced. Hill and Tatum have both continued successful careers in the intervening years, with Hill focusing more on dramatic roles and directing, while Tatum has appeared in action films and the Magic Mike franchise.

The project remains in early development, with no production timeline or release date announced. The talks with the original stars represent preliminary discussions rather than finalized deals. Sony Pictures has not commented on the status of the screenplay or who will direct the film.

cards.headline: BIGBANG Announces 31-Show World Stadium Tour for 20th Anniversary
cards.teaser: The K-pop group will bring G-Dragon, Taeyang, and Daesung together for performances across Asia, North America, Europe, and Australia.
cards.body:
BIGBANG is reuniting for a 31-show world stadium tour celebrating two decades since their debut. The tour will bring together members G-Dragon, Taeyang, and Daesung for performances spanning Asia, North America, Europe, and Australia.

The ambitious tour marks a significant comeback for the influential K-pop group, demonstrating their enduring appeal across global markets. The choice of stadium venues underscores BIGBANG's continued status as one of the most commercially successful acts in the industry.

cards.headline: Wu-Tang Clan Performs at NBA Finals Halftime Show
cards.teaser: The Staten Island hip-hop group performed during halftime of Game 4 between the Knicks and Spurs at Madison Square Garden.
cards.body:
Wu-Tang Clan performed the halftime show during Game 4 of the NBA Finals between the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs. The performance took place at Madison Square Garden with the Spurs holding a large lead at halftime.

The Staten Island natives brought a local connection to the New York venue. The group's appearance added to the high-profile entertainment surrounding the finals game, which drew numerous celebrities and cultural figures to the arena.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift Attends NBA Finals Game at Madison Square Garden
cards.teaser: The singer watched the Knicks face the Spurs in Game 4 of the NBA Finals, wearing a Stevie Knicks shirt with members of Haim.
cards.body:
Taylor Swift attended Game 4 of the NBA Finals between the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs at Madison Square Garden. The Knicks pulled off a remarkable 29-point comeback—the largest in NBA Finals history—to win 107-106 and take a 3-1 series lead.

Swift was among numerous celebrities courtside for the historic game, joining Spike Lee, Adam Sandler, Ben Stiller, Larry David, Timothée Chalamet, and Cardi B in the stands.

cards.headline: Indian Microdrama Platform Tadka Reaches 100 Million Users
cards.teaser: The short-form content platform within JioHotstar has grown daily watch time per viewer fivefold since launch.
cards.body:
Tadka, the microdrama platform within Indian streaming service JioHotstar, has surpassed 100 million users. The platform specializes in short-form premium content, establishing the format as a mainstream entertainment category in India.

Daily watch time per viewer on Tadka has increased fivefold since the service launched. More than 42 percent of the platform's viewership comes from audiences under 24 years old, indicating strong appeal among younger demographics. The growth reflects rising interest in short-form video content adapted for mobile viewing.

cards.headline: Australian Production Films Supernatural Romance With Japanese Star Yamada Takayuki
cards.teaser: Tanabata: The Evening of the Seventh spans three historical periods from Edo-period Japan to 2027 Australia.
cards.body:
Australian production company Titantale Film is shooting Tanabata: The Evening of the Seventh, a supernatural romance drama starring Japanese actor Yamada Takayuki. The project is fully funded from Australia with production service partners in Japan.

The film spans three historical periods: Edo-period Japan, 1865 New South Wales, and 2027 Australia. The story follows three incarnations across these time periods. Production is currently underway with the Australian-Japanese collaboration representing a cross-border approach to independent filmmaking.

cards.headline: Knicks Fans Stage Rituals Outside Madison Square Garden Before Game 4
cards.teaser: Several people burned sage and copal outside the arena hours before the NBA Finals game, seeking to change the team's luck.
cards.body:
New York Knicks fans gathered outside Madison Square Garden on Wednesday afternoon, performing cleansing rituals with copal and sage ahead of Game 4 against the San Antonio Spurs. The fans, dressed in team colors, aimed to manifest better luck for the hometown squad.

The spiritual practices reflected deep fan investment in the series. That evening, the Knicks mounted a remarkable comeback, overcoming a 29-point deficit—the largest turnaround in NBA Finals history—to win 107-106. The victory gave New York a 3-1 series lead over the Spurs.

hero.headline: Agriculture secretary rejects senator's call for screwworm vaccine
hero.teaser: Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins declined a request from Senate Judiciary Chair Chuck Grassley to develop a vaccine for parasites that returned to the U.S. after 60 years.
hero.body:
Senate Judiciary Chair Chuck Grassley urged Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins to develop a vaccine for New World screwworms after the parasite returned to the United States for the first time in six decades. Grassley said he had discussed the vaccine proposal with Rollins months before the recent outbreak confirmed in Texas.

Rollins rejected the suggestion from the Iowa Republican. The New World screwworm is a parasite that infests livestock and other animals, causing significant damage to agricultural operations.

The screwworm outbreak marks a major concern for the nation's cattle industry. The parasite was confirmed in a calf in south Texas, approximately 50 miles from the Mexico border, late last week. The last confirmed detection in Texas occurred in 1966. Federal officials have warned livestock owners for over a year about the parasite's progression through Mexico, where it has advanced more than 1,100 miles northward.

The screwworm fly's larvae feed on the blood of warm-blooded animals. While the risk to humans remains low, the parasite spreads quickly where large numbers of cattle and livestock are kept together. It was eliminated from the United States in the 1970s after causing tens of millions of dollars in losses.

Rollins defended her agency's response, insisting there is no threat of widespread infestation. She stated the Texas case represents the only confirmed detection so far and expressed confidence that the outbreak will not become established in the country. The agriculture secretary emphasized the flies pose no threat to food safety, though officials worry about potential shortages if the parasite takes hold in cattle and poultry populations.

In March, Rollins announced the USDA partnered with the Army Corps of Engineers and private company Mortenson Construction to build a new sterile fly production facility at Moore Airbase in Edinburg, Texas. This facility will support efforts to combat the spread.

The existing strategy relies on releasing sterile flies rather than vaccination. Female screwworm flies mate only once during their months-long lives, and eggs from sterile fly partners do not hatch. This approach significantly reduces the screwworm fly population over time.

Texas Agriculture Commissioner Sid Miller urged the Trump administration to intensify deployment of the screwworm adult suppression system, which combines attractants, bait, and targeted insecticides to reduce adult populations before sterile fly releases complete the eradication effort. Miller noted this approach was successfully deployed during previous eradication campaigns.

Past eradication efforts proved so effective that the United States closed its domestic facilities for breeding sterile flies, leaving only one facility in Panama. In Mexico, the high cost of medicines to treat screwworm cases has forced ranchers to use crude homemade measures, such as applying gasoline or lime to open wounds to remove the worms.

cards.headline: Trump urges Republicans to pass third reconciliation bill with $350 billion for Pentagon
cards.teaser: The president called on Congress to advance a new spending package that includes funding for the Department of Defense and elections legislation.
cards.body:
President Trump endorsed a third reconciliation bill on Wednesday, urging Congress to immediately pass the $350 billion package. The president called the measure Reconciliation 3.0 and said it should include the Save America Act.

Trump said the bill was requested by the Department of War, referring to the Department of Defense. The reconciliation process allows the Senate to pass budget-related legislation with a simple majority rather than the usual 60-vote threshold required to overcome a filibuster.

cards.headline: Trump casts doubt on renewing U.S.-Mexico-Canada trade agreement
cards.teaser: The president said he may not renew the USMCA, the trade deal he negotiated during his first term to replace NAFTA.
cards.body:
President Trump said Wednesday he may not renew the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement, the free trade deal he created during his first term as a replacement for NAFTA. Trump told reporters he was not looking to extend the pact.

The USMCA sets the terms of trade between the three North American countries and was a major accomplishment of Trump's initial presidency. The agreement includes a review process that permits the countries to renegotiate or exit the deal.

cards.headline: Inflation rises 4.2 percent over past year
cards.teaser: Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer criticized the Trump administration after new Labor Department data showed continued price increases.
cards.body:
The consumer price index jumped to 4.2 percent annually in May, marking a three-year high. This represents the third consecutive monthly increase since the start of the Iran war, which has driven up gasoline prices significantly. Before the conflict began, inflation stood at 2.4 percent.

President Trump responded to the report by saying he was not concerned about the rising inflation rates given recent developments in the conflict. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer attributed the price increases to Trump administration policies, using the term "Trumpflation" to describe current economic conditions.

cards.headline: U.S. conducts second night of strikes on Iran
cards.teaser: The U.S.
cards.body:
The U.S. military launched a second round of strikes against Iran on Wednesday, targeting multiple Iranian cities as negotiations over the war remained stalled. The strikes followed an initial assault the previous day.

Iran responded with drone attacks on Gulf states in retaliation. The escalating exchange of strikes between Washington and Tehran comes as Iran continues to assert control over the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global energy supplies.

cards.headline: NASA administrator defends all-male crew for Artemis III mission
cards.teaser: Jared Isaacman responded to criticism about the lack of female astronauts on the upcoming moon mission.
cards.body:
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman acknowledged public backlash over the all-male crew selection for Artemis III, noting reactions ranging from disappointment to outrage. The mission is scheduled to launch in 2027.

The four-person crew includes NASA astronauts Randy Bresnik, Frank Rubio, and Andre Douglas, along with Luca Parmitano from the European Space Agency. They will orbit Earth while practicing docking procedures with lunar landers as part of NASA's plan to return astronauts to the moon.

cards.headline: More than half of House Democrats behind on party dues
cards.teaser: An internal report shows average payment rates at 47 percent as some members threaten to withhold contributions over primary intervention.
cards.body:
More than half of House Democrats had paid less than 50 percent of their expected dues to the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee as of early April. The average payment rate stood at 47 percent, with nearly 30 members who are not in battleground districts paying nothing at all.

Some House Democrats have threatened to withhold dues unless the DCCC stops intervening in primary races. Member dues represent a significant portion of the committee's funding.
